page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual-socket Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory provisioning includes 1536 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware configuration is rounded out by 22800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD instance storage and a 600 Gbps network bandwidth baseline.

Benchmark data demonstrates massive multi-threaded scalability alongside high memory throughput. The server records top-tier multi-core performance in stress-ng at 411655.51 points and multi-threaded decompression at 2171.83 GB/sec, complemented by an uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 1168 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, it achieves 506.53 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 157.07 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-threaded performance exhibits modest figures, with stress-ng single-core in the middle 50% and single-thread gzip compression rating lower, reflecting architectural prioritization of aggregate core density over extreme individual core clocking.

Eliminating hypervisor overhead through its bare-metal architecture, the m8idn.metal-96xl yields substantial resource consolidation efficiency for distributed systems. The integration of 22.8 TB of NVMe local storage paired with 600 Gbps networking minimizes I/O bottlenecks. While CPU-only text generation speed scales moderately for large language models, prompt processing benefits from AMX matrix extensions. This instance profile is optimal for memory-intensive in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, massive parallel data pipelines, high-density container virtualization, and enterprise batch processing.
